effects.original_title: The CD47-signal regulatory protein alpha (SIRPa) interaction is a therapeutic target for human solid tumors
effects.original_authors: Willingham, SB; Volkmer, JP; Gentles, AJ; Sahoo, D; Dalerba, P; Mitra, SS; Wang, J; Contreras-Trujillo, H; Martin, R; Cohen, JD; Lovelace, P; Scheeren, FA; Chao, MP; Weiskopf, K; Tang, C; Volkmer, AK; Naik, TJ; Storm, TA; Mosley, AR; Edris, B
effects.original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
effects.replication_study: Syngeneic MT1A2 orthotopic breast tumor experiment in FVB mice (Figure 2, Figure 3 meta-analysis)
effects.description: In an immune-competent syngeneic MT1A2 breast cancer model, anti-CD47 antibody treatment significantly reduced final tumor weight compared with IgG isotype control (Figure 6A,B).
effects.citation_sentence: We sought to independently replicate the safety and efficacy of targeting CD47 in immune competent mice using a syngeneic model of breast cancer. This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 6A–C of Willingham et al. (2012).
effects.evidence: Results; Figure 2/3; Abstract: "The weight of tumors after 30 days administration of anti-CD47 antibodies or IgG isotype control were not found to be statistically significant different, whereas the original study reported inhibition of tumor growth with anti-CD47 treatment (Figure 6A,B; Willingham et al., 2012). However, our efforts to replicate this experiment were confounded because spontaneous regression of tumors occurred in several of the mice." Welch's t(9.66) = 1.796, p=0.104 (anti-CD47 mean 0.163 g > IgG 0.075 g); Glass' Δ original 2.54 vs replication −1.13, 95% CI [−2.35, 0.16].
effects.notes: Replication point estimate is in the opposite direction but non-significant, so not a reversal. Strong case for failure (null, opposite direction, replication CI excludes the original estimate, significant heterogeneity Q p=0.0039). Coded inconclusive because the authors never say 'failed to replicate' and instead state the attempt was 'confounded' by spontaneous tumor regression (wording added at editors' request; the decision letter suggested calling it 'inconclusive'); codebook tiebreaker failure-vs-inconclusive -> inconclusive. A second coder could reasonably code failure. Only one of the original's two antibody clones (MIAP410) was tested. Tumor volume curves (Fig 2-S1) are the same claim/experiment, not a separate entry. Original authors listed in the reference with initials only, truncated 'et al.' after Edris B.

effects.original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
effects.replication_study: Syngeneic MT1A2 orthotopic breast tumor experiment in FVB mice — histopathology of excised tumors (Table 1)
effects.outcome: Lymphocytic (inflammatory cell) infiltration of tumors, H&E histology
effects.contrast: anti-CD47 vs IgG isotype control treated tumors
effects.timepoint: End of treatment (study day 31, excised tumors)
effects.description: Anti-CD47 treatment increased lymphocytic/inflammatory cell infiltration at the tumor site, whereas IgG-treated tumors showed sparse lymphocytic infiltrate (Figure 6C).
effects.citation_sentence: Using a syngeneic breast cancer model, mouse anti-CD47 antibody treatment resulted in a statistically significant decrease in final tumor weight compared to IgG isotype control (Willingham et al., 2012). Anti-CD47 treatment also increased lymphocytic infiltration to the tumor site without unacceptable toxicity except short-term anemia observed immediately after dosing.
effects.evidence: Results, Table 1: "Both IgG and anti-CD47 treated tumors resulted in minimal to moderate lymphocytic infiltrate (Table 1)." Abstract: "We found IgG and anti-CD47 treated tumors resulted in minimal to moderate lymphocytic infiltrate, while the original study observed sparse lymphocytic infiltrate in IgG-treated tumors and increased inflammatory cell infiltrates in anti-CD47 treated tumors (Figure 6C ...)."
effects.notes: Descriptive comparison only, no statistical test. Lymphocytic infiltrate was the planned measure and showed no difference between arms (IgG: 6 minimal/1 moderate; CD47: 5 minimal/1 moderate) -> failure. Competing reading: the original's phrasing 'increased inflammatory cell infiltrates' could be partially supported by the unplanned neutrophil scoring ('neutrophilic infiltration was slightly increased in anti-CD47 treated tumors'), which would argue inconclusive. Replication used a predefined scoring system (Demaria et al., 2001) unlike the original — minor method change; authors call the replication direct. Same tumors as the tumor-weight entry, which was confounded by spontaneous regression.

effects.original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
effects.replication_study: Hematological toxicity analysis in the same FVB mouse experiment (Figure 1)
effects.outcome: Blood toxicity: red blood cell count, hemoglobin, hematocrit (short-term anemia) and other hematology parameters
effects.contrast: anti-CD47 vs IgG isotype control vs untreated baseline
effects.timepoint: 5 days after start of antibody injections
effects.description: Anti-CD47 antibody treatment caused no unacceptable hematological toxicity apart from short-term anemia shortly after dosing (Table S4, Supplemental Figure 6).
effects.citation_sentence: In the original study, BALB/c mice were analyzed for blood toxicity 5 days after two 500 µg antibody injections (Table S4) and C57BL/6 mice were analyzed for specific hematology parameters 1, 3, and 6 days after a single intraperitoneal injection of 250 µg of IgG or anti-CD47 antibodies (Supplemental Figure 6) (Willingham et al., 2012). Similar to what was reported for C57BL/6 mice in the original paper, FVB mice treated with anti-CD47 resulted in short-term anemia (Figure 1; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
effects.evidence: Results, Figure 1G–I: RBC F(2,17)=424.9, Hb F(2,17)=502.1, HCT F(2,17)=283.0, all Bonferroni-significant, "all slightly reduced in anti-CD47 treated mice compared to untreated and IgG treated mice." Abstract: "resulted in short-term anemia compared to controls, consistent with the previously described function of CD47 in normal phagocytosis of aging red blood cells and results reported in the original study (Table S4; Willingham et al., 2012)."
effects.notes: Authors explicitly call the anemia consistent with the original. Some non-anemia parameters also differed (WBC, lymphocytes, MCV, RDW significant after Bonferroni; mild monocytosis in 3 animals) but the authors do not frame these as contradicting the original's safety claim. replication_type: authors call the overall study a 'direct replication', but for toxicity they state 'This differed from the original study, which analyzed toxicity in different mouse strains and treatment regimens' (FVB vs BALB/c/C57BL/6; 400 µg every other day intratumoral vs 500 µg x2 or 250 µg i.p.) — both strain (context) and regimen (method) changed, so close extension; direct is a defensible alternative. Replication measured 15 parameters vs the original's 13 (granulocytes split into three types).
